title: Affine pushforward base change is bijective on affine sections
statement: For an affine morphism f and a quasi-coherent module F, the base-change map is bijective on sections over every affine open of S'.

proof.text: Choose affine charts U and W with W contained in the inverse image of U. The chart-coordinate theorem identifies the two section modules with tensor products and computes the base-change map on pure tensors.

Compose TensorProduct.comm, AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange, TensorProduct.congr and Algebra.TensorProduct.commRight to obtain the additive tensor reassociation equivalence; their pure-tensor formulas give r tensor m ↦ (r tensor 1) tensor m. TensorProduct.induction_on then identifies the coordinate map with this equivalence, proving chartwise bijectivity.

exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset and Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd show that the compatible affine charts form a basis of S'. Apply TopCat.Sheaf.isIso_iff_isIso_basis to the underlying additive sheaf morphism, using ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective on the basis. ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso then proves bijectivity on every open, hence on every affine open V.

lean.statement:
theorem affinePushforward_baseChange_app_bijective {X S X' S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) [IsAffineHom f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ∀ V : S'.Opens, IsAffineOpen V →
      Function.Bijective ((moduleBaseChangeMap f f' g g' sq.w F).app V)
